result.title: Certified Robustness via Sparse Second-Order Cone Relaxations
result.summary: Certified robustness is critical for deploying neural networks in safety-sensitive settings, but computing exact certificates typically requires solving nonconvex optimization problems. Practical verifiers use convex relaxations: linear programming (LP) relaxations are scalable but often too conservative, whereas semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxations can be substantially tighter but are computationally expensive. We introduce a hierarchy of second-order cone programming (SOCP) relaxations that provide stronger certificates than LP while avoiding the cost of global positive-semidefinite constraints. Our construction combines convex-hull relaxations of ReLU activations, selective McCormick lifting over certified variable bounds, and second-order cone constraints induced by 2-by-2 principal minors. Adding these constraints progressively yields a monotone hierarchy of increasingly tight bounds with a controllable computation-tightness trade-off. On fully connected and convolutional networks on MNIST and CIFAR-10, SOCP-based verification improves certified robust accuracy over LP-based verification and is competitive with alpha,beta-CROWN, while remaining orders of magnitude faster than SDP-based verification. These results position selective second-order constraints as a practical middle ground between scalable LP-based and tight SDP-based certification. Finally, we introduce class-optimized robust evaluation (CORE), which applies tighter relaxations only to target classes not certified by cheaper ones. On the fully connected MNIST benchmark, CORE variants match SDP-cert's certified robust accuracy while reducing average verification time by up to 86.30%.

AI.brief_summary: 提出一族二阶锥（SOCP）松弛，用于神经网络的鲁棒性认证，通过选择性 McCormick 提升与 2×2 主子式约束在 LP 与 SDP 之间取得计算与紧致度的折中，并提出只对未认证目标类别使用更紧松弛的 CORE 评估流程。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究对象是分类网络的对抗鲁棒性证书，不涉及视觉或多模态推理的内部状态、证据使用与停止决策；松弛层级与 CORE 的分级认证只是最泛化的「计算—精度」权衡，未提供可供核查的 LVR 迁移线索。
